scientific.integrity: The parity theorem is proved from boundary values of a reciprocal sine product, residue jumps, elementary quadratic Diophantine bounds, and weighted-simplex counting. Finite checks are used only as reproducibility sanity checks, not as proof of the infinite statement.
limitations: The theorem is for the explicit square-root generator family; arbitrary irrational generators can fail the polynomial coefficient bounds used for temperedness.

The full primary PDF of arXiv:2608.09354v1 was not retrievable through the accessible route; the abstract and a detailed public full-text reading were inspected, leaving a residual risk about unindexed remarks in the source.
The odd cases are crystalline-type distributions rather than strict crystalline measures because derivatives of the delta distribution occur at the origin.

title: Exact parity dichotomy for sine-product semigroup spectra
